This app has become a money grab.
I have used this app for a long time, but the current version is extremely disappointing.
The biggest issue is the subscription trap. I signed up for a trial expecting a trial experience, but I was charged afterward without a clear enough reminder. I have reported this to Apple because this kind of payment experience is not acceptable.
What makes it worse is that the app itself is getting worse every year. The workouts are outdated, repetitive, and lack creativity. It feels like the team is recycling old content instead of creating new and useful fitness programs. For a paid fitness app, the lack of fresh content is unacceptable.
I also noticed that critical reviews disappear, which makes me question how much the company values honest user feedback.
This app used to have potential, but now it feels like the priority is getting subscriptions rather than delivering a quality fitness experience.
Save your money and look for a better fitness app.

author: Riali.
title: Why is there such a string focus on losing weight?
content:
I used to use this app for a while and it worked okay, but stopped working out and tried to redownload it.

Why. Is. There. Such. A. Strong. Emphasis. On. Weight. Loss!?

You can’t even log in and use the app without setting a weight loss goal! Every single exercise comes with a note on how much weight you’ll lose. I understand it’s useful if you ARE trying to lose weight, but the app SPECIFICALLY ASKS what your goals are (disappointed to find out that increasing flexibility wasn’t an option, but I guess it’s a little niche) and never once did I include weight loss. 

I think it’s toxic (and this is more critique of diet culture as whole rather than the app itself) to assume every goddamn person tying to stay fit is trying to lose weight. I just want to be healthy, not feel pressured into losing weight when I’m already at a healthy one.

And, in the end, I don’t particularly care too much, I just deleted the app again, but what about the teenagers using this app? (There is a specific option when you log in to state you are under 18.) I don’t think it’s healthy to subject teenagers to that constant pressure, or worse, someone who has already struggled with EDs or an obsession with weight loss/appearance.

It’s one thing for the option to be there, in fact, I think it’s great for those who need or want it, but the way that this is constantly shoved down your throat is ridiculous. The creators are (or at should be) fully aware that losing weight isn’t the only reason to work out, so why don’t they act like it?

Look around and see how many other companies have done the same and gotten away with minimal pushback. Stop rolling over and letting them. Previously 7/10, now absolute 0/10 will never recommend again unless they backtrack on this within the next couple of updates. I am NOT going to stop screaming about this. It’s just crazy how a women’s workout app doesn’t even accommodate to pregnant women as much as you would expect them to. Very strange but simple fix yeah? author: MarieShouse
title: Many options of exercise!
content: I have enjoyed this app so far! I stopped exercising a few years ago and now started having some chronic back pain back from old injury and I knew losing weight and get better shape was the only (& the best) option I can maintain better back. This app gave me very easy start and am looking forward to more exercise and I can’t wait to start seeing my body changing!

author: Dahliadaydreams
title: So misogynistic and fat shaming
content: The onboarding process is shocking. I was expecting something supportive of women and empowering. This app blatantly targets insecurities. Instead of being full of photos of real women and a diversity of bodies, it has AI bodies (🙄) with exaggerated chests and butts. It asks directly "do you want to be attractive?" The blatant anti fat bias is vile. So extremely disappointed and will be putting my money toward a different app that doesn't reinforce every terrible manipulation and stereotype out there. I'm guessing this app was developed by men. It sure feels that way.
